title: When Less Is More: Content Strategies for Subscription Video on Demand
authors: Miguel Godinho de Matos; Samir Mamadehussene; Pedro Ferreira
eligible_reason: Randomized field experiment with a common timing, not staggered adoption. TELCO subscribers are randomly assigned to drip (gradual, exp_period = stage_1) versus all-at-once release of recommended shows; the main panel has two periods (time 0/1). Main-text regressions (paper_replication_final.Rmd) are logit (feglm/glm) and Poisson (fepois) models of visits, subscriptions, completions and number of episodes on drip, period and drip x period, with exp_rec or uid FE. Single treatment date, randomized assignment, nonlinear models.
design_notes: R Markdown (fixest feglm/fepois, glm). Synthetic data in tb.replication_data.RData (tb.panel_dataset, tb.panel_visits, tb.panel_watching_detail, tb.panel_dataset_expanded).
data_files_note: mksc-read-me.htm: original TELCO data under NDA; 'the data provided here is a synthetic dataset designed to replicate the main findings', variables derived from originals with noise, some tables from a subsample.
data_provenance_note: Synthetic (noise-perturbed) data stated in the read-me.
screener_notes: Screened from package read-me and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). RCT with one release date; nonlinear models; synthetic data.
